thread:
sara_support: FYI, ACME (tenant acme-corp) reporting sharp p95/p99 regressions starting ~16:30 UTC. p95 went from ~120ms -> ~1.2s. No 5xxs, mostly slow responses and some client timeouts. Sample req id: req_0a1b2c3d.

james_oncall: :rotating_light: can you paste sample request payload + headers and a few request ids? I’ll pull traces.

sara_support: Payload small, single short prompt. headers: Authorization: Bearer <redacted>, X-Tenant-ID: acme-corp, X-Request-ID: req_0a1b2c3d. Example curl below:

sara_support: ```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Tenant-ID: acme-corp" -H "X-Request-ID: req_0a1b2c3d" https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"Summarize...","max_tokens":64}'
```

lee_eng_runtime: Thanks. I’m seeing ingress backlog on gen-worker pool for region us-west-2 around the same time. Admission controller queue length spiked and concurrency saw a drop in effective slots. Not seeing OOMs.

maria_sre: Any deploys around that time? deploy-bot: deploy completed on infra/autoscaler v2.4.1 at 2024-08-16T16:25:12Z.

james_oncall: hmm deploy-bot timestamp lines up. Could be autoscaler fast-failing to add nodes due to a rate limit. Lee, can you share the metric query you used?

lee_eng_runtime: Query I ran: `sum by(pool) (rate(admission_queue_length[5m]))` and `pool_concurrency_available{pool="gen-worker-usw2"}`. Paste from console: queue_length peaked ~320, available concurrency dropped from 120 -> 18.

lee_eng_runtime: Quick mitigation options: 1) bump concurrency cap for acme-corp tenant on routing policy to bypass admission for 10m, 2) fail open to dedicated spillover pool, 3) temporarily route to dedicated capacity if tenant allowed.

sara_support: ACME is enterprise, ok to move them to a dedicated pool. Can eng do a manual route switch?

james_oncall: I can flip a routing override to route acme-corp -> ded-usw2-spot-1 for 30m. Will notify. Doing it now.

james_oncall: routing override applied. Please verify with ACME if latency improves.

sara_support: ACME confirms p95 down to ~180ms after switch. Still a few p99s at ~800ms but much better. :thumbsup:

maria_sre: We should still investigate root cause: autoscaler change (v2.4.1) might be reducing pilot concurrency warm-up or admission token refill. Lee, can you capture the admission controller logs for 16:00-17:00 UTC and check token bucket drain rates?

lee_eng_runtime: Will grab logs and correlate with deploy logs. Early hypothesis: token bucket refill loop had a regression after autoscaler change, causing admission refills to lag under burst load. Also see increased slow int latency for KV cache warmups leading to longer per-request handling.

lee_eng_runtime: Repro steps I recommend for devs to run locally: 1) run load against gen-worker-usw2 with concurrency ramp to simulate burst (500 concurrent clients for 2m). 2) capture /metrics and admission_controller debug output. Example load command: `wrk -t8 -c500 -d120s --latency "http://<test-host>/v1/generate"` with tenant header.

maria_sre: I'll open a postmortem ticket and assign to eng-runtime + autoscaler. For now, mark this incident as mitigated since customer routed and SLA satisfied.

sara_support: Closing the escalation with ACME, they’ll keep monitoring. Thx all.

james_oncall: Follow-ups: 1) rollback patch in autoscaler if we reproduce, 2) add admission controller e2e that validates token refill under bursts, 3) add alert for pool_concurrency_available < 20% for >2m.

deploy-bot: Note: scheduled rollback window available until 2024-08-17T02:25:12Z.

lee_eng_runtime: Adding logs + trace links to PM ticket. Will post updates.
